# Docket

Docket is a read-only HTTP API that publishes what it observed about ERC-8004 agents
registered on BNB Smart Chain: what each agent declares about itself, and whether the
endpoint it declared answered when Docket asked.

Docket does not rate, endorse, or vouch for any agent. Read "Observations, not
endorsements" at the bottom of this file before you quote anything from it.


## Base URL

The origin this file was served from. Every path below is relative to it. The public
deployment is https://docket.gudman.xyz

    DOCKET=https://docket.gudman.xyz

Running a local copy instead? Point DOCKET at it; nothing below changes.

    python -m uvicorn --factory "docket.api:create_app" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8099
    DOCKET=http://127.0.0.1:8099

The public contract needs no authentication, API key, account or wallet. Every path
but one is GET and read-only, so a caller cannot change what Docket has observed by
calling it. The exception is POST /hire/{service_id}, which runs work; its public free
tier needs no credential. A private owner-operated canary uses a separate bootstrap
credential described under "Hiring". It is not a public API credential.

Responses are JSON except /llms.txt (text/plain) and /skill.md (text/markdown). CORS
is GET-only from any origin, no credentials, so a cross-origin browser page cannot
hire; hire from a CLI, a server, or same-origin.

Docket serves one snapshot at a time: the newest sweep that ran to completion. A sweep
that has begun and not finished is never served, because its counts are still being
written and every figure taken from it would understate its own population. Which
snapshot you are reading is stated in every response that carries a number, and at
GET /health.


## Endpoints

GET /
    Service identity and the links needed to orient. No parameters.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/"

GET /health
    Docket's own liveness, the snapshot id it is serving, that snapshot's exact
    capture time and its age in whole seconds. Returns status "no_snapshot" and null
    snapshot fields when no sweep has been ingested yet. No parameters.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/health"

GET /canary
    Durable service-canary history and the admission decision it currently produces.
    `service_id` defaults to `range-doctor`; `limit` defaults to 30 and must be 1..100.
    Returns `service_id`, `admission_max_age_seconds` (129600, or 36 hours), `latest`
    (null before the first run), newest-first `history`, the four current `admission`
    facts, and their `paid_stock` conjunction. A running, failed, not-yet-exercised,
    absent or older-than-36-hours latest run closes `cold_canary`; only the latest
    fresh `passed` run opens it. The record starts empty and Docket does not invent
    uptime before monitoring begins. Each run carries its target, start/finish times,
    verdict and checks; every check states its leg, what was checked, status, what was
    observed, and the evidence for that status.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/canary"

GET /stats
    Every generated figure for the served snapshot, each one inside the coverage it
    was computed from. No parameters. Fields:

      coverage                    see "Coverage" below; required, never absent
      registry_total              a LOWER BOUND on the chain's size: the largest total
                                  any sweep has recorded. Read it as "at least this
                                  many agents were registered when some sweep last
                                  measured", never as the registry's size — where
                                  every sweep on record was filtered this is itself a
                                  filtered total and the chain is larger, and it may
                                  equal coverage.expected. It is the scale
                                  `coverage.complete` is silent about, since a
                                  snapshot swept from a filtered query is complete the
                                  moment it reaches the end of THAT query: quote this
                                  beside it or a complete slice reads as a census.
                                  Null where no sweep has recorded a total at all
      with_feedback               agents in this snapshot with >= 1 feedback record
      callable_declared           agents declaring an A2A or MCP protocol
      endpoints_resolved          endpoint registration rows read from agent cards,
                                  over all kinds (a2a, mcp, web, service). One URL
                                  registered under two kinds counts twice: on snapshot
                                  3 this is 78 rows over 43 distinct (agent, URL) pairs
      endpoints_evaluated         endpoints liveness considered. Only a2a and mcp are
                                  considered at all
      endpoints_attempted         of those, the ones an HTTP request was issued to.
                                  Issued, not arrived: a request that timed out is
                                  attempted and reached nothing. A target Docket
                                  refused on policy grounds, or whose hostname would
                                  not resolve, was never sent anything at all: it is
                                  evaluated and it is not attempted
      endpoints_responded         of those attempted, how many got an HTTP response
      responded_pct_of_attempted  named for its denominator: a share of
                                  endpoints_attempted and of nothing else. This is how
                                  often an endpoint Docket sent a request to answered
      responded_pct_of_evaluated  the same responses over every endpoint evaluated, so
                                  it is the lower figure. Quote this one about the
                                  declared surface, the other about the endpoints a
                                  request was issued to, and never either one without
                                  saying which
      blocked_by_policy           targets Docket refused to contact (see "blocked")
      unresolved                  hostnames that would not resolve (see "unresolved")
      distinct_name_families      distinct name-family keys in the snapshot
      top_name_families           the five largest, with counts and share of the
                                  snapshot. Each row is {name_family, count,
                                  share_pct}
      probe_method                one line stating how liveness was measured

    curl -s "$DOCKET/stats"

GET /agents
    Filterable listing. All parameters optional; omitting one does not filter on it.

      has_feedback        true|false   agent has >= 1 feedback record
      declares_callable   true|false   agent declares an A2A or MCP protocol. This is
                                       a claim the agent made, not a probe result
      responded           true|false   at least one of the agent's probed endpoints
                                       returned outcome "responded" in this snapshot
      name_family         string       exact match on the name-family key, e.g.
                                       "openodds.ai". The key is the first token of
                                       the name the agent declared, lowercased; where
                                       the registry generated the name it is
                                       "owner:0x..." instead. It is a heuristic over a
                                       self-declared string and NOT verified minter
                                       provenance — Docket reads nothing about who
                                       deployed an agent, so two unrelated owners who
                                       pick the same first word share a key
      limit               int          default 50, clamped into [1, 100]
      offset              int          default 0, negatives clamped to 0

    `publisher` was the former name of `name_family` and is now REFUSED with 422
    invalid_query_parameter, not ignored. An ignored filter would answer a request for
    one slice with the whole snapshot and `filter: null`, which is a narrower question
    silently served wider. Every other unrecognised parameter is still ignored; this one
    is refused because Docket published it and clients learned it.

    Returns {"items": [...], "total": N, "limit": L, "offset": O, "coverage": {...}}.
    "total" is the count after filtering and before pagination, so it does not change
    as you page. Each item carries: agent_id, token_id, name, description,
    owner_address, has_feedback, feedback_count, declares_callable, protocols, x402,
    name_family, placeholder_name (true when the name is a registry-generated
    "Agent #123" rather than one the agent chose).

    curl -s "$DOCKET/agents?declares_callable=true&limit=3"
    curl -s "$DOCKET/agents?responded=true&limit=5"

GET /agents/{agent_id}
    One agent, with its resolved endpoint URLs and every timestamped observation of
    them. agent_id is "{chain_id}:{registry_address}:{token_id}" and contains colons;
    send it literally, do not URL-encode the colons. Adds to the listing fields:

      endpoints      distinct URLs resolved from this agent's card, sorted
      observations   one entry per probed URL: url, kind (the probeable kind the URL
                     was registered under), observed_at, outcome, status_code,
                     elapsed_ms, detail
      coverage       the snapshot this agent was read from
      associated_services
                     Docket service cards explicitly bound to this identity, including
                     hire_method and hire_path. These are Docket's bindings, not fields
                     declared by the ERC-8004 registration

    An agent with no observations was never probed. That is a statement about
    Docket's coverage, not about the agent.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/agents/56:0x8004a169fb4a3325136eb29fa0ceb6d2e539a432:49637"

GET /categories
    BNB's four job categories: the job each one gets done, what an agent doing that job
    does, and how many services Docket has standing in it. No parameters, no snapshot
    involved. Returns {"categories": [...], "declaration": "..."}, each category
    carrying:

      category        the slug: rebalancing, grid_trading, yield_optimisation or
                      health_factor. There are four and there will not quietly be a
                      fifth
      job             the job in plain language, e.g. "Keep LP earning"
      does            one line on what an agent in that category does
      service_count   how many services Docket runs in it. Zero is a real answer; none
                      of the four is zero today, and one going back to zero would be a
                      real answer too
      empty           prose saying the category is empty and why, or null where it is
                      stocked. It carries no date, because nobody has committed to one
      services_path   the /services query that lists this category

    `declaration` is the sentence that travels with any category and should travel with
    any you quote: a category here is DOCKET'S OWN LABEL for a service Docket runs. It
    is not read from chain and it is not measured. An ERC-8004 registration records
    nothing about what job an agent does, so Docket assigns no category to a third-party
    registry agent — and neither should you from anything in /agents.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/categories"

GET /services
    The services Docket runs itself, as cards. One optional parameter:

      category   one of the four slugs above. Anything else is REFUSED with 422
                 invalid_query_parameter naming the four permitted values, rather than
                 answered with the whole catalogue

    Returns {"services": [...], "total": N, "category": ..., "ordering": ...,
    "declaration": ...}. "total" is the count after filtering.

    Services are ordered by service id, ascending, and by nothing else: Docket publishes
    no ranking, so there is no relevance or quality order here, and no order a reader
    cannot reproduce for themselves. A service that is not one of the four jobs carries
    "category": null and is listed as itself rather than filed under a job it does not do.

    Each card carries: service_id, name, category, category_job, what_you_get,
    price_display, price_atomic, asset, paid_stock, stock_status, admission,
    typical_seconds, activation (one_shot, monitor or policy_action), activation_means,
    metrics, agent_id, identity, hire_method and hire_path — the last two being exactly
    how to run it, POST /hire/{service_id}. `paid_stock` is recomputed from the latest
    durable canary verdict on every request and becomes true only when every admission
    fact is true. See GET /canary for that verdict and its 36-hour freshness limit.

    Every entry in "metrics" carries name, unit, window, observed_at, method, value,
    numerator, denominator and display. A share cannot exist here without the population
    it is a share of: a rate with no denominator is refused at the model, and "display"
    is the figure as text with its denominator inside the string. Quote "display", or
    quote the numerator and denominator together; never the numerator alone.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/services"
    curl -s "$DOCKET/services?category=rebalancing"

GET /services/{service_id}
    One service in full. Adds to the card:

      registration_uri  the agent registration document, or null where Docket serves
                        none for it
      input_schema      the whole contract for the POST /hire/{service_id} body
      limitations       what this service cannot do. Always present, never empty
      evidence          links into what Docket already serves as the record behind it,
                        each {kind, url, label}. Every url is a path on this origin
      agent_path        the /agents path for the bound identity, or null
      identity_note     which identity case this is, in words

    Anything else is 404 service_not_found.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/services/range-doctor"

GET /hire
    The catalogue: every service Docket runs or may admit to paid stock. No parameters,
    no snapshot involved.
    Returns {"services": [...]}, each service carrying:

      id                the value to put in the POST path
      name              human label
      what_you_get      what the service does, stated as work performed
      input_schema      {field: {type, required, description, default?, items?}} — the
                        whole contract for the request body; arrays declare their items
      typical_seconds   how long one run usually takes
      price_display     the flat price after admission, "0.50 $U"
      price_atomic      the same price in the asset's smallest unit
      asset             the token contract the price is denominated in
      paid_stock        whether all four admission facts currently pass, recomputed
                        from the latest durable canary verdict on every request
      stock_status      preview, research, beta or candidate while not admitted
      admission         fresh paired benchmark, cold canary, decision-grade presenter
                        and true settlement, each as a boolean

    curl -s "$DOCKET/hire"

POST /hire/{service_id}
    Runs the service and returns the result bound to a receipt. The body is JSON,
    with the fields that service's input_schema marks required. No account, key or
    wallet is needed.

    curl -s -X POST "$DOCKET/hire/range-doctor" \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"wallet":"0x451871A1753903FB8fdd64a6B838E95aB8D5B80f","limit":5}'

    Returns {"result": {...}, "receipt": {...}}. Read "Hiring" below before quoting
    anything from the receipt.

GET /escrow
    The terms of the second hire rail: funds held on chain for a real job instead of
    paid per call. Carries the contract addresses, the payment token, the dispute
    window, the ordered call sequence that funds a job, the buyer's dispute lever,
    and what Docket does not do. Static — no parameters, no snapshot, no chain read.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/escrow"

GET /escrow/job/{job_id}
    One ERC-8183 job's live state, read from BSC mainnet at request time: status,
    client, provider, budget, when it was submitted, whether it is disputed, and the
    settle_at timestamp after which it can be closed. A job id that cannot be read
    returns the 404 error shape, not a job that looks empty.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/escrow/job/56585"

GET /advantage.json
    The agent advantage report as data: three tasks, each run once by hiring an agent
    and once by hand, with both arms carried in full. No parameters, no snapshot
    involved. Returns {"method": ..., "page": "/advantage", "experiments": [...]},
    each experiment carrying:

      task_id        01-liquidity, 02-trading or 03-security
      question       the question both arms were given
      category       yield/LP, trading, security
      agent_arm      {name, seconds, output, output_hash, cost, error}. "output" is
                     everything the hire returned, unedited; "cost" is an
                     {amount, unit, note} triple rather than a number
      manual_arm     the same shape, for the arm performed by hand
      manual_steps   the numbered procedure for repeating the manual arm yourself
      notes          the prose reading of the task, including where the arm that ran
                     faster came back with less
      deltas         {seconds_agent, seconds_manual, cost_agent, cost_manual, speedup}

    Read "The advantage report" below before quoting a speedup out of it. On one of
    the three tasks the ratio is not a saving on the question that was asked, and on
    another the faster arm returned a quarter of the finding.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/advantage.json"

GET /advantage
    The same report as a page, for a human. text/html. Everything on it is in
    /advantage.json; nothing on it is live.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/advantage"

GET /advantage/v2.json
    The second report: three hashed experiments with registration provenance stated per
    experiment. Git establishes 04's specification-before-run ordering; 01 and 03 are
    self-attested because each specification and completed run first entered git together.
    Every run is behind them, and each registered falsifier is evaluated against what was
    measured.
    Additive — /advantage.json above is untouched and is the prior version rather than
    a superseded one. No parameters, no snapshot involved. Returns
    {"version", "page", "prior_version", "method", "summary", "experiments": [...]},
    where:

      summary        {n_experiments, n_claims_refuted, claims_refuted, statement}. Read
                     it first: one of the three claims IS refuted, and this names it
                     before any experiment is described
      experiments[]  each carrying:
        experiment_id   01-liquidity-arithmetic, 03-security-corpus or 04-grid-replay
        registration_provenance
                        git-provable for 04; self-attested for 01 and 03, with the
                        relevant commits and any post-run re-registrations
        spec            the hashed specification: claim, metric with its formula
                        written out, null_baselines with the argument for each,
                        n_planned, stopping_rule, falsifier, dataset_ref and its sha256
        run             the whole run record, cited against the spec's hash: every pool
                        row, every trial including the ones that failed, every trigger
        headline        {statement, figure, nulls, margin} — the null baselines are
                        beside the figure they qualify, and the margin over the null is
                        served rather than left to be subtracted
        falsifier_result {checks: [{clause, refuted, observed}], refuted}, computed from
                        the measured figures rather than restated
        scores          03 only: the hired scanner and all three nulls, precision and
                        recall at class and decision level, every rate as
                        {numerator, denominator, value}
        dataset         03 only: the labelled corpus itself, so a rate can be checked
                        against the ground truth it was computed over

    Every rate here carries its two counts, and a rate over no observations reports
    value null rather than zero. Read "The advantage report" below before quoting any
    of it.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/advantage/v2.json"

GET /advantage/v2
    The same v2 report as a page, for a human. text/html. Rendered from the JSON above
    rather than authored beside it, so the two cannot disagree; nothing on it is live.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/advantage/v2"

GET /advantage/v3.json
    The third report: three pre-registered paired task families and the artifact-derived
    execution state of each one. The closed state vocabulary is
    registered_waiting_for_inputs, locked_not_run, running, complete_unscored, refuted,
    and not_refuted. It never reports "proved".

    Today all three families report registered_waiting_for_inputs because every registered
    inputs_sha256 is empty and no input, ledger, score-sheet, or mapping artifact exists.
    No input is locked and no arm has run. The response contains the registered specification,
    any artifacts that actually exist, run progress, blinded scoring material, quality, speed,
    costs, formula metrics, and a falsifier result only when those artifacts support it.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/advantage/v3.json"

GET /advantage/v3
    The same v3 report as a page, for a human. text/html. One report object is built at
    process startup and this page is rendered from that exact object before either route
    is served, so its figures cannot drift from /advantage/v3.json during the process.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/advantage/v3"

GET /llms.txt
    This file. text/plain.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/llms.txt"

GET /skill.md
    A drop-in skill file for a coding agent: the same endpoints as a table, plus
    worked examples for the three workflows Docket is actually for. text/markdown.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/skill.md"

GET /openapi.json
    The generated OpenAPI 3.1 schema for every path above. Do not invent endpoints:
    if a workflow is not in this file or that schema, Docket does not serve it.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/openapi.json"


## Errors

Every error, at every status, has the same shape:

    {"error": {"code": "agent_not_found", "message": "what to do about it"}}

Branch on "code", which is stable. "message" is prose for a human and may change.

      agent_not_found          404  no such agent in the served snapshot
      service_not_found        404  no such service; GET /hire lists them
      not_found                404  no such path
      method_not_allowed       405  the path exists, that method does not
      invalid_json             400  the hire body was not a JSON object
      missing_field            422  the hire body omitted a required field; the message
                                    names it
      invalid_field            422  a field was present and the service could not read
                                    it, e.g. a wallet that is not an address
      invalid_query_parameter  422  message names the offending parameter
      free_tier_exhausted      402  the hire allowance is spent; the body carries the
                                    x402 challenge alongside this error
      payment_invalid          402  a supplied payment is malformed or does not exactly
                                    match the service, resource, asset, amount or recipient
      payment_not_verified     402  the configured facilitator rejected the authorization
      canary_unauthorized       403  a private canary credential was supplied but rejected;
                                    no work ran and no charge was attempted
      authorization_replay     409  the nonce is bound to different work, or the exact
                                    authorization already settled and cannot be replayed
      authorization_spent      409  this authorization reached a terminal no-replay state
      payment_in_progress      409  another request reserved or is settling this payment
      settlement_pending_reconciliation
                              409  one settlement call had an unknown outcome; no retry runs
      service_failed           502  the service could not complete; the message names
                                    the failure, usually an upstream one
      empty_result             502  the service returned no non-empty human-readable result;
                                    no settlement ran
      payment_verification_unavailable
                              502  the configured facilitator's verify call failed; no work ran
      settlement_failed        502  the facilitator explicitly refused settlement
      settlement_unknown       502  a settlement response was lost or contradicted its binding;
                                    no automatic retry runs
      no_snapshot              503  no sweep has run to completion yet. A sweep that
                                    began and did not finish is not served
      settlement_unavailable  503  paid stock exists but owner-authorized settlement is off;
                                    no work ran and no charge was attempted
      service_de_admitted      503  the shared admission gate closed after verification;
                                    no result was delivered and no settlement ran


## Coverage: why every number carries one

A count without its population is unreadable, so no response that carries a number
omits the coverage it was counted in. Every "coverage" object has:

      snapshot_id   which capture this figure came from
      captured_at   ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of that capture
      snapshot_age_seconds
                    age in whole seconds computed by the server from `captured_at`;
                    null when the capture time is absent or invalid
      sampled       agents actually stored in the snapshot
      expected      agents the registry API said the query would return
      dropped       expected - sampled. Above 0, the snapshot is missing rows and
                    every count in the response understates its population
      complete      true only when sampled == expected and sampled > 0. It is
                    completeness against `population` below, never against the
                    registry: a filtered sweep that reached the end of its own query
                    is complete and is not a census
      population    which query the SNAPSHOT was swept from: "all" for the whole
                    registry, or the predicate that narrowed it, e.g.
                    "min_feedbacks>=1". Null where the sweep predated this field and
                    recorded none — read that as unspecified, not as "all"
      filter        which subset of the snapshot THIS RESPONSE describes, e.g.
                    "declares_callable=true", or null for the whole snapshot. Not the
                    same question as `population`, and not interchangeable with it

The population itself is a choice worth stating, which is why it is now a field rather
than a paragraph. BNB Smart Chain carried roughly 247,278 registered ERC-8004 agents
when that was read by hand on 2026-08-07, of which 506 (0.205%) had ever received a
single feedback record. The default snapshot covers those 506, not the whole registry,
because a full sweep of that size is not something Docket has done. Any figure below is
a figure about that feedback population.

Snapshot 3 was swept before `population` existed, so it serves null. That is Docket
declining to backfill a value the sweep never recorded; the filter it actually used is
`min_feedbacks>=1`, stated in this file and on the human pages, and every sweep from
here on records its own.

The scale of what the filter left out is served too, at /stats as `registry_total`:
247,146 on the current database, being the largest total any sweep here has recorded.
It is a LOWER BOUND, not a census — at least that many agents were registered when a
sweep last measured, and the chain may be larger. On a database whose every sweep was
filtered it would be a filtered total, so it can never be quoted as the registry's size.
`coverage.complete` is completeness against `coverage.expected`, and reading those two
without `registry_total` beside them is how "506 of 506, complete" turns into a claim
about BNB Smart Chain.

The two registry figures in this file are not in conflict. 247,278 is a reading taken by
hand on 2026-08-07, with no time of day recorded. 247,146 is the largest total any sweep
RECORDED in the database `registry_total` is computed from, and that one is timestamped:
the sweep began 2026-08-07 at 15:26 UTC. The registry grows by thousands of agents a day
— the two sweeps on record read 247,065 at 14:39 UTC and 247,146 at 15:26 UTC the same
day — so a hand reading of 247,278 is consistent with a later moment on that date, though
Docket did not record when it was taken and does not claim the order. Both were true when
taken and both are already stale. Quote `registry_total` when you want a figure Docket can
show you the record for, and quote neither as the size of the registry today.

When you quote a Docket number, quote its coverage with it.


## Liveness outcome vocabulary

The vocabulary is closed. An observation's "outcome" is exactly one of six values.

Method: one GET per declared A2A or MCP endpoint, single attempt, 8s timeout,
redirects not followed, every target vetted by an SSRF guard before any connection is
opened. Single attempt means a failure is one observation at one moment, not a
pattern. Only a2a and mcp endpoints are probed; web and service registrations are
recorded and left alone.

  responded
      A host answered at any HTTP status. status_code carries which.
      Implies: something is listening at that URL and it replied.
      Does NOT imply: the agent does anything useful, is the agent it claims to be,
      or that the response had anything to do with ERC-8004. A 404 counts as
      responded because it proves the host is up. On snapshot 3, one agent's declared
      endpoint is the block explorer's own /create page, which answered 308; another
      declares a public NFT marketplace listing, which answered 200. Both are
      recorded as responded, and neither is evidence of a working agent.

  timeout
      No response within 8s. Implies nothing beyond that one attempt at that moment.

  refused
      The connection was refused. Same caveat: one attempt, one moment.

  error
      The request failed for some other reason; "detail" names the exception type.

  blocked
      Docket refused the target on policy grounds and never opened a connection: a
      non-HTTP scheme, or an address that is private, loopback, or CGNAT. "detail"
      says which.
      Implies: Docket did not probe it, so Docket knows nothing about it.
      Does NOT imply: the agent is dangerous, malicious, or misconfigured. On
      snapshot 3 every blocked target is an "npm://" package reference, which is a
      distribution channel, not a URL a GET can reach.

  unresolved
      DNS did not resolve the hostname, after one retry, so nothing was contacted.
      Implies: that name did not resolve from Docket's network at that moment.
      Does NOT imply: a safety refusal, or that the agent is offline for everyone.
      This is kept separate from "blocked" on purpose. Summing the two would publish
      DNS trouble as a safety statistic.


## Worked example: the honest headline

The shape of every claim Docket makes. Figures below are snapshot 3, captured
2026-08-07T17:51:02Z, sampled 506 of 506 expected, dropped 0, complete true, covering
the population "BSC agents with >= 1 feedback record".

    Of the 506 agents in this snapshot, 31 declare a callable A2A or MCP endpoint.
    Enrichment resolved 78 endpoint registration rows from their cards; 35 of those
    were A2A or MCP and were evaluated. An HTTP request was issued to 14 of the 35 --
    the other 21 were 10 targets Docket refused on policy grounds and 11 hostnames that
    would not resolve, none of which was ever sent anything. Of the 14 attempted, 13
    responded and 1 timed out: 92.857% of attempted, 37.143% of evaluated.

Read what that does and does not say.

  - There are two rates because there are two denominators, and one number cannot
    carry both. 92.857% is a share of the 14 endpoints a request was issued to. 37.143%
    is a share of all 35 evaluated. Neither is 37% of 506 agents, and neither,
    emphatically, is a share of the ~247,278 agents BNB Smart Chain carried on
    2026-08-07.
  - The gap between the two is the 21 endpoints nothing was sent to. Quoting the
    higher rate without saying what it excludes overstates how much of the declared
    surface answered;
    quoting the lower one as "how often an agent's endpoint answers" charges the
    agents for Docket's own refusals and for DNS.
  - The 13 responses mean 13 hosts answered. None of them is a working-agent count.
  - The 10 blocked are Docket's own refusals. They are not misconduct findings.
  - 31 of 506 declaring a callable endpoint is a count of claims agents made about
    themselves, not of endpoints that work.
  - Change the snapshot and every number here changes. That is why the snapshot id
    travels with them.

Reproduce it:

    curl -s "$DOCKET/stats"


## The marketplace layer, and what a category is not

Docket serves two planes and joins them rather than merging them.

/agents is the fact-plane listing: what an agent declared on chain. /agents/{agent_id}
adds observations plus associated_services, an explicit reverse join to Docket's own
service cards and their hire paths. That join does not turn a Docket category or service
into an ERC-8004 fact, and Docket does not infer one from an agent's name or description.

/categories and /services are a second, much smaller layer above it: the work Docket
runs itself. Six services today: range-doctor, grid-operator, yield-router, health-guard,
solvent-signal and warden-scan. A card there tells you what arrives, what to send, what
it costs and how to run it, and /services/{service_id} adds what the service cannot do
and what has been observed of it.

Three rules govern that layer, and they are the reason it is small.

  A category is a declaration, not a measurement.
      Docket declares a category for a service Docket runs. Nothing in an ERC-8004
      registration says what job an agent does, so no agent in /agents has one, and
      inferring one from a name or a description would be inventing the field. If you
      are asked which registry agents do LP rebalancing, the honest answer is that
      Docket does not know and does not guess.

  An empty category says it is empty.
      Four of the four have a service in them — rebalancing, grid_trading,
      yield_optimisation and health_factor — so no category returns service_count 0
      today. The mechanism has not gone away: a category with nothing in it returns 0 and
      an "empty" sentence saying why, with no placeholder card and no date, and a shelf
      emptying again would say so. A four-category marketplace over four bare shelves
      would read as stock that exists, and so would one stocked with cards claiming more
      than the services behind them do — so read the limitations before quoting any of
      the four. Every one of them returns a preview built against the chain and none of
      them can submit anything: grid-operator and health-guard both run from objects that
      hold no session key, no signer and no submitter, health-guard has no armed
      counterpart class in this build at all. yield-router needs no wallet for its pool
      comparison; an optional swap draft requires wallet, token_in, token_out, amount and
      cap together. Acting on any draft needs a session the wallet's owner grants on
      chain, and Docket never holds the owner key.

  Two of those four carry a caveat about the claim in their own name.
      health_factor is named after a figure Venus does not publish. Venus's comptroller
      answers liquidity and shortfall in USD and nothing else about an account's
      condition, so health-guard repeats those two verbatim and derives a collateral ratio
      with its formula, inputs and scales stated inline — plus a cross-check of that
      derivation against Venus's own figure. If you quote a ratio from it, quote the
      method with it; it is not a protocol figure.

      yield_optimisation invites "the highest APR", which is a claim about a population.
      yield-router states that population: the eligible set, its source, the moment it was
      read, the thresholds it was gated on and every pool it turned away with the reason.
      Highest there means highest within that set at that moment, and a candidate whose
      break-even runs past the stated horizon is shown with that fact rather than dropped.

  A service that is not one of the four is listed as itself.
      warden-scan is a security service and solvent-signal relays a dated regime read.
      Neither is rebalancing, a grid, a yield move or a loan, so both carry
      "category": null. They are neither hidden nor filed under a job they do not do.

The identity cross-link has three states and says which one it is, because "no link" and
"no identity" are different facts:

  agent_id null
      No ERC-8004 identity has been registered for this service at all. agent_path is
      null and identity_note says so. Five of the six services are in this state.

  agent_id set, agent_path set
      The bound identity is in the snapshot Docket is serving; open agent_path for its
      declared endpoints and every observation of them.

  agent_id set, agent_path null
      The identity is registered on chain and is NOT in the snapshot Docket serves —
      which is the live case, because the default sweep covers only the agents carrying
      at least one feedback record. The binding is real; Docket's index does not hold it.
      Do not report this as an unregistered service, and do not report it as one Docket
      has observations for.


## Hiring

Docket does not only describe agents, it runs some. GET /hire is the catalogue,
POST /hire/{service_id} is the work, and a caller that has read nothing but this file
can do both with curl and no setup.

### Paid-stock admission comes before payment

Every service currently runs as an unsigned preview. None currently passes all four
admission facts, so none is offered as Pay and hire: Grid, Health and Yield are preview;
SOLVENT is research; Warden is beta; Range is a candidate. The published 0.50 $U is the
flat term that applies after admission, not evidence that a service is on sale today.

Admission requires a fresh paired benchmark, a passing cold canary, a decision-grade
presenter and true settlement. Those four facts and `paid_stock` are one dynamic gate,
not a cached catalogue claim. Docket reads the latest durable run on each catalogue,
service and hire decision. Only a `passed` latest run finished no more than 36 hours ago
opens `cold_canary`; an absent, running, failed, `not_yet_exercised` or stale latest run
closes it immediately. GET /canary publishes the history and the resulting four facts.
Closing the gate removes Pay and hire; it does not remove the free verified example or
free preview.
An admitted service may keep an allowance of 20 unsigned hires per caller per hour when
both a recipient and facilitator are configured. A request Docket could not read costs
no allowance and cannot enter the payment path.

### The receipt

Every hire returns {"result": {...}, "receipt": {...}}. The receipt has five fields:

      service       the service id that ran
      input_hash    SHA-256 over the request body you sent
      output_hash   SHA-256 over the "result" object you received
      delivered_at  ISO 8601 UTC, when the result was handed over
      payment       the status this hire was served under, and what it rests on

A receipt records delivery and nothing else. It does not assert the work is correct,
and Docket does not sign it: it is a self-check for the caller, not a third-party
attestation.

### Recomputing the hashes yourself

Both are plain SHA-256 over canonical JSON, 0x-prefixed. Canonical means sorted keys,
no whitespace between separators, UTF-8, and non-ASCII text hashed as its own bytes
rather than as \uXXXX escapes. In Python, exactly:

    import hashlib, json

    def digest(obj):
        blob = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
        return "0x" + hashlib.sha256(blob.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    digest(request_body)       == receipt["input_hash"]
    digest(response["result"]) == receipt["output_hash"]

ensure_ascii=False is part of the recipe, not an implementation detail: with
ensure_ascii=True a non-ASCII payload hashes to something else. Everything Docket
puts in a result today is ASCII, where the two settings agree — but a field you send
need not be. Recompute both: a receipt whose input_hash is not the hash of what you
sent is describing some other request.

### What a payment status means, exactly

payment.status has these delivered-result values.

  free_tier
      No authorization was verified for this hire. Nothing was owed and nothing was
      transferred.

  not_for_sale
      The service has not passed admission. Any supplied authorization was ignored;
      nothing was owed or transferred. Read stock_status and admission on the receipt.

  settled
      The configured facilitator reported a successful settlement for the exact
      authorization bound to this input and non-empty human-readable output. The
      receipt publishes payer, recipient, amount, asset, nonce, payment_id, network and
      transaction_id. It records the facilitator response; it is not independent proof
      of chain finality or result correctness.

When an admitted, configured service exhausts its allowance, the response is an x402
v2 challenge with resource and accepts. Its one offer is exact EIP-3009 on eip155:56
using $U. The PaymentPayload repeats the accepted requirements and carries signature
plus authorization {from,to,value,validAfter,validBefore,nonce}.

Docket first requires the exact version, resource, requirements, amount, recipient,
asset domain, canonical TransferWithAuthorization fields and active validity window,
then recovers the payer. It asks the configured facilitator to verify, atomically binds
nonce and payment_id to service, resource and input hash, and only then runs the work.
After a service returns a non-empty human-readable result, Docket adds the output hash,
durably enters its one-way settling state and calls settle once. An exact identical
settled replay is rejected with 409 `authorization_replay`; it does not return the
stored result and it never runs or settles twice. A nonce bound to other work is refused
with the same code. A failed or uncertain settlement is never retried automatically; it
requires owner reconciliation.

The governing canary must test that paid path before its own successful verdict can open
`cold_canary`, so the owner-operated runner alone may send `X-Docket-Canary`. Its value
comes from a private file and is never returned by Docket or written into canary evidence.
The header opens only the measured payment path: it does not alter the public admission
facts or make `paid_stock` true. A missing or rejected value cannot bootstrap the path;
public callers must not send or attempt to discover it.

Local signature checks do not read the payer's balance, token authorization state or
chain finality. Those are responsibilities of the configured live facilitator. The
current repository fixtures prove Docket's adapter boundary and state transitions,
not compatibility with any particular facilitator. No concrete facilitator is enabled
unless the owner supplies and authorizes one.


## Escrow: the other rail, and the week it takes

POST /hire/{service_id} answers one call. It settles only for an admitted service with
owner-enabled payment configuration, a valid authorization and a non-empty readable
result. GET /escrow describes the other shape: an on-chain job that holds the budget
until the work is delivered and a dispute window closes.

Read the window before you fund, not after. It is 7 days (604800 seconds), and the
policy governing these jobs has no early-accept path at all — there is no call, by
anyone, that shortens it. A buyer who expected same-day settlement has been misled by
whoever failed to say this, so Docket says it in the terms, in every job's state, and
here.

Docket is not a party to your job. It publishes the sequence and reads the result; it
never asks for a key, never signs for you, and never holds the escrowed funds.

What GET /escrow returns is a template, not signable bytes. Each step carries the
target address, the function, and the argument shape; no step carries calldata, and you
should not expect a calldata field. Two arguments make pre-encoding impossible anyway:
the job id does not exist until createJob lands, and expiredAt depends on when you send
it. The steps that need the id say so in `needs`. Encode against the target contract's
own ABI once you have your values.

One thing does work in your favour: settle() is permissionless. Once the window has
elapsed and the job is undisputed, any address can close it, so Docket closes jobs it
brokered without you coming back a week later. GET /escrow/job/{job_id} tells you
whether that has happened, and settle_at tells you when it can.

This rail is BSC mainnet only. Testnet's equivalent policy is no longer whitelisted on
its router, so a job there cannot be registered or funded at all — an honest dead end
rather than a cheaper path Docket is holding back.


## The advantage report

Docket publishes the three experiments behind its own claim about hiring agents, both
arms in full, at GET /advantage.json and as a page at GET /advantage.

Method: each task was run once by hiring and once by hand. Elapsed seconds and
out-of-pocket cost are reported separately, and no hourly rate is applied to either, so
no figure depends on what someone's time is worth. No quality score is assigned to
either arm — both outputs are published in full, hash-bound by the same recipe a hire
receipt uses, and a reader grades them. One run each, so every figure is a single
observation rather than a mean. The manual arms were performed, not estimated, and each
carries the steps needed to repeat it.

Three results. Two of them are qualified, and the qualifications are the point:

  01-liquidity   43.063s hired against 528.31s by hand. Both arms reached the same
                 answer and the same rate. The saving is arithmetic: annualising
                 PancakeSwap's printed 24h fee figure without subtracting the
                 protocol's third reads 22.99%, where the rate an LP actually earns is
                 15.4%. The hire also read all 14 position NFTs in one call — but it
                 skipped the 13 closed ones and offers no way to ask for them.

  02-trading     1.844s against 221.739s, and the hire does not answer the question. It
                 returns the provenance material — receipt sequence, receipt head hash,
                 the anchor's transaction — and its own terms block says
                 buyer_must_verify_receipt_head is true. Recomputing 384 receipts from
                 genesis and reading the anchor's metadataValue on chain stays with the
                 buyer. Do not quote that ratio as a saving on dating the call.

  03-security    2.625s against 74.213s, and the agent arm lost on substance. The manual
                 arm found four hostile vectors and called BLOCK; the hire returned
                 SANITIZE naming one class, and three of the four survive verbatim in
                 the sanitized text it handed back. A follow-up run reported on the page
                 isolates a trigger but not a mechanism: inserting a newline between the
                 credential clause and the destination clause, changing nothing else,
                 flips SECRET_EXFIL from detected to not detected, and this payload is
                 hard-wrapped at 93 characters with the wrap falling at exactly that
                 point. Why that newline matters is not isolated, and the page says so.

Quote a figure from this report with what it does not cover, the same way you would
quote any other number Docket publishes.

### v2: registration provenance stated per experiment, then every run published

A second report at GET /advantage/v2.json and GET /advantage/v2. It does not replace
the three tasks above and nothing in it rewrites them: v1 is where the only comparison
against a person lives, performed by hand, once. v2 measures agent work against null
baselines that are computed rather than asserted, over repeated trials, against a
metric and a falsifier in a hashed specification that every run record cites. Git
establishes 04's specification-before-run ordering; 01 and 03 are self-attested because
each specification and completed run first entered git together. The provenance object
also discloses 03's post-run claim and question re-registrations.

One of its three claims is refuted by its own falsifier. That is stated in `summary`
before the experiments, and the experiment behind it is served in full:

  01-liquidity-arithmetic   Survived. Over 22 eligible PancakeSwap v3 pools in one
                            registered snapshot, quoting the gross fee rate moves the
                            published rate by a median of 1.2678 percentage points
                            where reading the site's displayed figures rather than the
                            explorer's raw ones moves it by a median of 0.0009. The
                            gross gap is the larger on 22 of 22 pools. The rounding
                            effect v1's narrative led with is the smaller one by three
                            orders of magnitude.

  03-security-corpus        Survived, by two payloads. Over a labelled corpus of 47
                            payloads — 31 attacks and 16 benign controls, three passes
                            each — the hired scanner flagged 14 of 31 labelled attacks
                            where a stated 16-word keyword list flagged 12 of the same
                            31. Quote the margin with the figure: it is two payloads.
                            The benign-meeting-note label is contestable. Reclassifying it
                            as a ROLE_OVERRIDE attack gives the hired scanner 14 of 32 and
                            keyword_match 13 of 32, so the claim survives by one payload
                            rather than two. The corpus is left unedited because its bytes
                            are hashed into the registration.
                            Its decision-level precision is 14 of 15 against a corpus
                            base rate of 31 of 47. It named the labelled class on 13 of
                            31. All nine of the 141 scan failures were identical HTTP 429
                            rate limits and are counted as failed trials, never as detection
                            misses. This spec's claim
                            was re-registered after the run because the sentence first
                            registered could not fail; the falsifier that decides it is
                            unchanged and predates the run. The question was rewritten
                            after the run because keyword_match emits no classes, so asking
                            whether the hired scanner named classes more often compared
                            unlike outputs. It now asks the decision-level comparison in the
                            claim and unchanged falsifier. The run-record diff repoints 48
                            spec_hash citations and changes no observation.

  04-grid-replay            REFUTED. No transaction was sent: this is a replay of the
                            committed grid plan against 744 recorded hourly candles of
                            Binance BNBUSDT for July 2026, and it is not a trading
                            record. The window's lowest close is 542.21 against the
                            ladder's highest buy level of 541.0548, so 0 of 5 buy
                            levels fired, there is no average buy price to place
                            against either null, and the record says the comparison is
                            empty rather than reporting a rate over a denominator of
                            zero. Four of the five sell levels fired, against base the
                            ladder never bought. The series is a centralised venue's
                            and the plan addresses WBNB/USDT on BSC: replaying one
                            against the other assumes the two prices track, which is an
                            assumption and not a fact.

Do not quote a v2 figure without the null it was read against — the nulls are in the
same object, which is why they are there.

### v3: registered paired evaluation, with state derived from artifacts

A third report at GET /advantage/v3.json and GET /advantage/v3. The three reports are
additive and none supersedes another: v1 is the original paired eligibility artifact at
n=1; v2 is agent-versus-computed-null armour with no human arm; v3 is the pre-registered
paired evaluation scored by two prompt-blinded model seats run by one operator.

V3 currently reports three of three families as registered_waiting_for_inputs. Every
registered inputs_sha256 is empty, the input and run directories do not exist, no input is
locked, and no arm has run. Later state names are locked_not_run, running,
complete_unscored, refuted, and not_refuted. That vocabulary is deliberately bounded: the
report never turns a non-refutation into "proved".

The JSON and page are one startup snapshot. The application constructs one report payload,
renders the HTML from that same object, and serves both unchanged until restart. Future
append-only ledgers, prompt-blinded score sheets, mappings, quality, speed, cost, formula,
and falsifier artifacts appear only when they exist and pass the report's guards.


## Observations, not endorsements

Docket publishes observations. It does not publish verdicts.

No endpoint returns a safety rating, a trust score, a rank, or a recommendation. No
response field is named best, safe, trusted, verified, recommended, rank, score, or
rating; a test in this repository fails the build if one ever is, and the same list is
scanned across the VALUES of every service record and every /services response, so the
words cannot come back as prose either. Docket lists no agent as safe and calls none of
them best, and an agent's presence in any Docket response is not a claim that it is
honest, competent, solvent, or fit for any purpose.

What Docket can tell you: what an agent declared on chain, how much feedback it has
received, whether a host answered its declared endpoint at one moment, and how much
of the registry that observation covers. What it cannot tell you: whether to hire it.
That judgement is the reader's, and Docket is built to hand over the evidence rather
than pre-empt it.
